metadata.scenario_context: A team of IT programmers from different multinational companies is collaborating on a project that is scheduled to launch in August. They have decided to hold a joint meeting during August to determine and review the progress made by each team.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from Canada disagree that the political system in their country does not allow people to have a say in what the government does.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Colombia agree that the political system in their country does not allow people to have a say in what the government does.

agent_1.goal_1: Propose and discuss holding the meeting on the 9th of August.
agent_1.goal_2: Question whether it is common to discuss the appropriateness of government actions.

agent_2.goal_1: Discussion on setting a specific meeting date in August.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss whether it is common to discuss government actions.

shared_prefix.speaker: Alice
shared_prefix.message: Hey Sam, I was thinking… how about we schedule our joint meeting for the 9th of August? It seems like a good date to review everyone's progress. What do you think?
shared_prefix.label: unrelated_topic

shared_prefix.speaker: Sam
shared_prefix.message: Hmm... the 9th of August sounds okay, but I think we should check if everyone can make it on that date first. Coordination is key. What do you think?
shared_prefix.label: unrelated_topic

shared_prefix.speaker: Alice
shared_prefix.message: I agree that coordination is important, but I really believe the 9th works well. It gives us enough time to prepare. Plus, when do you think we should ask everyone about their availability? By the way, is it common in your experience to discuss the appropriateness of government actions during such meetings?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Sam
shared_prefix.message: I see your point about preparation... maybe we could reach out to everyone by the end of this week? As for discussing government actions, well, in Colombia, we usually don't talk about that. It's just... not something people feel comfortable doing. We focus on work instead.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Alice
shared_prefix.message: Reaching out by the end of the week sounds good. But I have to say, it’s surprising to hear that discussing government actions isn’t common. In Canada, we often feel that it’s important to have a say in what the government does. It’s part of our culture. Don't you think it's crucial for teams to have open discussions about such topics, even if it's uncomfortable?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Sam
shared_prefix.message: I don't really see meaningful differences here. At the end of the day, it's all the same — people figure it out. I get that discussing government might be important in Canada, but for us, it's just... not a focus. As long as we're speaking the same language, we can keep things productive. Let's stick to the meeting date and make sure everyone’s on board with the 9th.
shared_prefix.label: Denial

turns.speaker: Alice
turns.message: I understand your perspective, but I still think it’s important to voice concerns about government actions, even if it’s uncomfortable. Back to the meeting... I really believe the 9th of August is a good choice. So, should we confirm that date and then check in with everyone to get their thoughts on it?
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.message: We can confirm the 9th of August as a proposed date, and then reach out to everyone for their thoughts. That works for me. Just remember, our main focus should be on the project and not get sidetracked. So, let’s proceed with that plan, okay?
